title: Simmons urges players to step up in absence of seniors in South Africa Test
excerpt: Bangladesh will be without Mushfiqur Rahim and Hasan Mahmud
author: Atif Azam
body: Bangladesh coach Phil Simmons has called on the rest of the squad to step up as the visitors prepare to take on South Africa in the second Test without Mushfiqur Rahim and Hasan Mahmud, both ruled out with injuries.

Hasan has been ruled out of the series-concluding Test at Centurion with tennis elbow, while Mushfiqur is unavailable after sustaining a groin injury ahead of the decider. Bangladesh trail 0-1 after losing the opening Test by nine wickets.

"We saw in the last two Test matches when the other senior player Mominul wasn't there, Hridoy could step up," Simmons said. "So that's how we are trying to work it, that whoever comes in for him will step up and do what we ask them to do. That's why they're here.
"Hasan is gone, but we have four other fast bowlers here, so somebody has to take his workload."
Simmons also said Bangladesh had backed Mominul Haque through his recent lean patch, with a decision on his place in the XI to be taken after Sunday's training session.
Mominul, who scored 13 Test centuries in his career, made scores of 0 and 1 in the opening Test. He has not registered a half-century in his last 10 innings and averages around 10 in South Africa.

"Sometimes we say that senior players, and players who've scored 13 Test hundreds, must know what they're doing in some way. So yes, he's struggled for a while, but again he's working hard, he's trying to get back that form. Sometimes you have to back players for a little bit longer," Simmons said.
"In this case, we have backed him. As I said, today we will sit down and decide what is to happen from tomorrow."
The Bangladesh coach also indicated that the team was yet to decide whether to field four fast bowlers, saying the composition would depend on the conditions and the balance they wanted to strike.

"We're going to decide today when we see the wicket. Yes, people come here and play four pacers, but that's the makeup of their team and that was the balance that helped them. So we have to look at the balance that helps the Bangladesh team in this Test match," he said.

Simmons identified the bowlers' lines and lengths as one of the key areas Bangladesh needed to improve after the opening Test. He felt they had not made the South African batters play often enough, particularly around the off stump and fourth-stump channels.

"I think the main lesson that we would have spoken about a lot is the lines that we bowl to them. We don't feel that we made them play enough, and that's one of the things that we have to improve on," he said.
"I think scoring 400 in the first innings is a great thing, coming from 120 for 5, so that's a good thing. We need to improve on how often we make the batsmen play on the off stump and fourth stump."
